# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 16 (Bu-Vb Np16)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The sixteenth rule of the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Vinaya Piṭaka is titled *Eḷakaloma* ("Carrying wool too far") [SuttaCentral]. It stipulates that a Buddhist monk who carries sheep's wool on an excessively long journey must relinquish the wool and formally confess the transgression [SuttaCentral]. A complete modern English translation of the rule and its exposition is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels to this rule are preserved widely across early Buddhist Vinaya traditions, including the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and Parivāra of the Pali Canon, as well as Vinaya texts and Prātimokṣa sūtras of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka (where it corresponds to rule 26), Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reflects extensive shared Vinaya phrasing across 81 Pali texts, demonstrating particularly strong formulaic matches with the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* sub-commentary (*Ṭīkā*) as well as procedural expositions in adjacent *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* rules such as Np 20, Np 13, Np 24, Np 4, and Np 5 [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistically, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with Tibetan Vinaya literature, including the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2), the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007), and Prātimokṣa commentaries such as the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus], in agreement with the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda parallels recorded by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
